opportunities.title: Observable transient follow-up
opportunities.outcome: A transient-science group can turn public candidates into an auditable observing plan before scarce observing time is allocated.
opportunities.uncertainty: How many physically feasible, science-useful visits survive priority, visibility and cadence constraints?
opportunities.action: Compile a site- and night-specific worklist with eligibility witnesses per visit.
opportunities.test: Independently recompute visibility, time conflicts and cadence. Compare with direct scheduling on identical candidates and slots.
opportunities.alternative: An existing broker plus an astronomer using a conventional scheduler, or the same scheduler used directly.
opportunities.scale: Batch new nights from public candidates; observatory priorities and availability still belong to their operators.
opportunities.economics: Count broker access, ephemerides, schedule validation, expert review, handoff and the cost of occupying a slot. No allocation, demand or revenue observed.

opportunities.title: Forecasts from incomplete observation streams
opportunities.outcome: Operators planning weather-sensitive field instruments could price the value of a forecast issued earlier from partial observations.
opportunities.uncertainty: Will the lead-time gain survive archive delay, missing sensors and station-level error?
opportunities.action: Build a shadow-mode replay of issue-time weather predictions and station observations.
opportunities.test: Freeze station/event splits and compare matched availability, error, missed windows and lead time against archived IFS/AIFS and persistence.
opportunities.alternative: Use existing IFS or AIFS forecasts and a conventional issue-time station replay.
opportunities.scale: Repeat across historical windows and sites with documented data rights; target-specific calibration and maintenance remain.
opportunities.economics: Compare cost per correctly identified usable window, including compute, station feeds, false alarms and human review. No local forecasting advantage measured.

opportunities.title: Independent checks of committed-model output
opportunities.outcome: An evaluator could check whether a reported token agrees with the greedy output of a committed integer model for the bound input, while the weights remain private.
opportunities.uncertainty: Can the evaluator authenticate the commitment, cover the needed tokens and justify the complete proving cost under the protocol assumptions?
opportunities.action: Check a genuine published sample with the upstream verifier and independently change each public input; request no paid service.
opportunities.test: Verify a genuine proof and reject altered bound public inputs. Separately measure total proof costs against rerunning the exact accessible reference model and check which tokens the proof covers.
opportunities.alternative: Upstream FlashProve verifier, direct rerun of accessible weights, or signed provider attestation with its weaker trust assumption.
opportunities.scale: Reuse one verifier across compatible commitments. Each supported model and numerical convention needs qualification.
opportunities.economics: Count proof production, verification, commitment distribution, transfer and support. A private-weight provider and a customer have not agreed to participate.

opportunities.title: Editable scientific instrument fixtures
opportunities.outcome: An instrumentation laboratory could generate and repeatedly revise bespoke passive mounting fixtures from dimensioned drawings.
opportunities.uncertainty: Do unseen parts rebuild with editable constraints, acceptable material tolerances and a safe engineering review?
opportunities.action: Construct native source models from unseen public drawings and request a controlled dimension change.
opportunities.test: Compare the CAD model and edited variant with direct parametric construction; independently inspect dimensions, constraint history and regeneration.
opportunities.alternative: An experienced CAD designer with a parametric library, or direct use of the public FreeCAD verifier and existing agents.
opportunities.scale: Reusable parametric families could spread design costs over variants. Physical qualification and excluded high-risk uses remain separate.
opportunities.economics: Include modeller time, rework, simulation or physical metrology, maintenance and responsibility for defects. No manufacturing order or adoption observed.

opportunities.title: Verified replacements for recurring numerical kernels
opportunities.outcome: A research-software group could amortize correctness-checked performance improvements across repeated simulations.
opportunities.uncertainty: Can an optimized kernel improve end-to-end time while preserving invariants across unseen architectures and data?
opportunities.action: Test one separable numerical kernel on an authorized CPU against a tuned library and compiler; count the search.
opportunities.test: Blind input families, precision and conservation checks; compare full workloads, compute crossover volume and stability.
opportunities.alternative: A tuned library with vectorization/BLAS, a conventional optimizer, existing AlphaEvolve if separately authorized, or keeping the current implementation.
opportunities.scale: Redistribute accepted replacements only under compatible licences; each new hardware target invalidates performance qualification.
opportunities.economics: Measure total search and integration costs, end-to-end CPU savings, verification, portability and support. No usage volume or net margin observed.
